Kavya Reddy
Senior Product Designer | Hyderabad, Telangana
kavya.reddy772@example.com | +91 9244242714

Product designer focused on end-to-end consumer experiences for food and delivery platforms. Skilled at translating user research into scalable design systems and high-conversion interfaces. Available to join after 30 days' notice.

Experience
UrbanPantry — Feb 2024 - Aug 2026
Senior Product Designer
- Led a cross-functional initiative to build a responsive Design Systems library in Figma, reducing new screen design time by 45% and improving component reuse across web and mobile.
- Designed and shipped a revamped onboarding flow using UI/UX best practices that increased first-week retention by 18% and reduced time-to-order by 22%.
- Partnered with product and engineering via Jira to scope and deliver 12 feature releases, maintaining a quarter-over-quarter bug regression rate under 3%.
- Conducted moderated usability tests and remote user interviews to validate concepts, resulting in a prioritized roadmap informed by User Research and measurable A/B outcomes.

Swiggy — Apr 2019 - Jan 2024
Product Designer
- Drove end-to-end UI/UX for a city expansion product, creating high-fidelity prototypes in Adobe XD and Figma that shortened stakeholder review cycles by 35%.
- Ran mixed-method User Research (surveys, contextual interviews) to identify friction in order tracking; redesigned tracking UI and improved NPS for tracking by 12 points.
- Contributed to the company-wide Design Systems, standardizing components and tokens that reduced visual inconsistencies by 60% across apps.
- Managed tickets and sprint priorities in Jira, collaborating with PMs and engineers to deliver 8 major launches with an average on-time delivery rate of 92%.

Projects
- Personal Design System: Maintained a Figma-based component library and documentation site used as a starter kit for freelance projects; includes tokens, accessibility checklist, and interaction specs.
- Quick Usability Toolkit: A reusable Adobe XD template and research script for rapid guerrilla testing, used to run 20+ 15-minute sessions with target users.
